name: Chamomile
habitat: Sunny disturbed ground, field margins, tracks, gravel, waste ground.
identify: Small white-rayed daisy heads about 2 cm across with a raised YELLOW CONE at the centre.
German chamomile's central cone is hollow when you cut it lengthways — the key separation from the useless look-alikes.
Crushed flowers smell sweetly of apple.

lookalikes.name: Scentless mayweed / stinking chamomile
lookalikes.danger: Low, but useless — and stinking chamomile is a skin irritant.
lookalikes.tell: Smell them. Real chamomile smells of apple; scentless mayweed smells of nothing and stinking chamomile smells acrid. The mayweed's centre is solid, not hollow.

lookalikes.name: Ox-eye daisy and other daisies
lookalikes.tell: Much larger flower heads on a single stem, with broad toothed spoon-shaped leaves rather than feathery ones.

preparations.method: Steep a good handful of flower heads in hot water, covered, for 10 minutes.
preparations.for_use: Settling the gut, calming, and a cooled wash for inflamed eyes and skin. Covering it matters — the active volatile oils leave with the steam.

preparations.method: Soak cloth in the cooled strong infusion.
preparations.for_use: Inflamed skin, sties, and irritated grazes.

cautions: Asteraceae family: real anaphylaxis has been reported in people with severe ragweed allergy.
Mildly anticoagulant in quantity — take care alongside blood thinners.
It soothes. It does not treat an infection.
evidence: Extensively used and reasonably well studied for topical inflammation and gut spasm; the anti-inflammatory constituents (bisabolol, chamazulene) are well characterised.
